notes.summary: In Sentence Rearrangement (para jumbles) four or more sentences P, Q, R, S are given out of order. Choose the sequence that makes a logical paragraph. Options look like QPSR, so you rarely need to solve fully — find one or two fixed links and eliminate.

concepts.title: Find the opening sentence
concepts.body: The first sentence introduces the topic and can stand alone. It usually names a person or thing in full (Mahatma Gandhi, The Himalayas). A sentence starting with He, This, However, Therefore, Such almost never opens the paragraph.

concepts.title: Find mandatory pairs
concepts.body:
Look for links that force two sentences together:
  • Pronoun → noun: it/he/they needs an earlier noun.
  • Article: a camera first, the camera later.
  • Connectors: However, But contrast the previous line; Therefore, As a result follow a cause.
  • Time order: first, then, finally; in 1990… by 2000.

concepts.title: Use the options
concepts.body: Once you know the opener or one pair (say R must come right after P), strike out every option without that feature. Often only one survives.

varieties.name: Four sentences P, Q, R, S
varieties.how: Find the opener, then one pronoun or connector link; eliminate options.

example.q:
P: However, it was rejected by the publisher.
Q: Ravi wrote his first novel at nineteen.
R: He then rewrote it completely.
S: The rewritten version became a bestseller.
steps: Q names Ravi in full → opener.
P (However, it…) contrasts with writing the novel → QP.
R (then rewrote) follows the rejection, S follows R.

varieties.name: First and last sentences given
varieties.how: Sentence 1 and 6 are fixed; arrange P, Q, R, S between them so the chain flows from 1 to 6.

example.q:
1: The kettle began to whistle.
P: She poured the water into a cup.
Q: Asha turned off the stove.
R: Then she added a tea bag.
S: Finally she stirred in some honey.
6: Her tea was ready.
steps: Pour (P), then tea bag (R), finally honey (S).

tips: Hunt for the opener first; it alone can eliminate half the options.
A sentence with 'the' plus a noun mentioned earlier with 'a' must come after that sentence.
Read your final sequence once quickly to confirm it flows.
traps: A sentence with a general statement may look like an opener but can also be a concluding summary — check for words like thus, hence, in short.
Do not force a time order if the paragraph is an argument; connectors matter more there.

questions.q:
Rearrange the parts to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: She saved a little money from her salary every month.
Q: Lata had always dreamed of owning a bicycle.
R: After a year, she finally had enough to buy one.
S: She rode it proudly to work the very next day.
questions.solution: Q introduces Lata and her dream (opener). P tells how she saved; R says after a year she had enough; S describes riding it. QPRS.

questions.q:
The first and last sentences are given. Rearrange P, Q, R, S.
1: The farmer woke up before sunrise.
P: Then he led the bullocks to the field.
Q: He fed his cattle and drank a glass of milk.
R: By noon, half the field had been ploughed.
S: There he began ploughing the dry soil.
6: He rested under a neem tree for lunch.
questions.solution: After waking, he feeds the cattle (Q), then leads bullocks to the field (P). There in S refers to the field → P before S. R (by noon) leads into lunch. QPSR.

questions.q:
Rearrange the parts to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: This made the old method of copying books by hand far less common.
Q: The printing press was developed in Europe in the fifteenth century.
R: As a result, more people learned to read.
S: It allowed books to be produced quickly and cheaply.
questions.solution: Q names the printing press (opener). S's It refers to the press. P's This refers to cheap production. R's As a result gives the final effect. QSPR.

questions.q:
Rearrange the parts to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: But the machine kept failing in the rainy season.
Q: The village bought a water pump to irrigate its fields.
R: The villagers finally replaced it with a solar-powered model.
S: For a few months, the pump worked well.
questions.solution: Q introduces the pump. S: it worked well at first. P: But contrasts with that success. R: finally replaced it. QSPR.

questions.q:
Rearrange the parts to form a meaningful paragraph.
P: Such habits, repeated daily, slowly change the brain's reward system.
Q: Many people check their phones dozens of times an hour.
R: Breaking the cycle therefore needs more than willpower; it needs a change of environment.
S: Each notification gives a small burst of pleasure that makes them check again.
questions.solution: Q states the general fact (opener). S explains why (them = many people). P's Such habits sums up Q and S. R's therefore draws the conclusion. QSPR.

questions.q:
The first and last sentences are given. Rearrange P, Q, R, S.
1: Mangroves grow along tropical coastlines where salt water meets land.
P: These roots also trap mud, slowly building new land.
Q: Their tangled roots break the force of waves during storms.
R: Despite these benefits, large areas have been cleared for fish farms.
S: Moreover, they shelter young fish and crabs.
6: Protecting the remaining forests is now an urgent task.
questions.solution: Q mentions tangled roots; P's These roots also continues it → QP. S's Moreover adds another benefit. R's Despite these benefits turns to the problem and leads to sentence 6. QPSR.

flashcards.front: Signs a sentence is NOT the opener
flashcards.back: Starts with a pronoun (he, it, this), or a connector (however, therefore, also, moreover).

flashcards.front: 'a X' vs 'the X' in para jumbles
flashcards.back: The sentence introducing 'a X' comes before the one mentioning 'the X'.
Find the opener + one mandatory pair, then eliminate options.
